source_text: Nihil ad innocentiam promovet modestia rei per ipsum genus nocentis sed ille a quo non refrenatur: nam ipsa per se ipsam rectissime omnino suis ipsis motibus accusatur, quibus ne excedat obsistitur. Non itaque, ut dicis
pass_a_gloss: Nothing to innocence promovet modestia guilty through itself genus harmful but that from whither not refrenatur: for herself through himself ipsam rectissime entirely his-own ipsis motibus accusatur, to-whom lest excedat obsistitur. not and-so, so-that/as you-say.
pass_b_english: Moderating a thing that harms by its very nature does nothing to advance innocence.

choices.why: Julian's forensic/moral fault tied to will, not a substance in nature.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded. Julian is not first-English.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Contra Iulianum / Against Julian), including authorities Julian quoted; Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
